**Restrict factorized evaluation to full-delta rounds.**

`factors::evaluate` rebuilds each factor relation on every round. `full_matches` uses `Scan::Full`, and each matching row is charged before it is added. Projection later classifies those already-built matches as `full`, `old`, or `new`; it does not avoid the full scan.

For a recursive factor plus an independent ground atom, partial-delta rounds can therefore enumerate the complete growing recursive join again. On a standard transitive-closure chain, this can raise the work from quadratic to cubic and exhaust the default join-step limit at a sufficiently large chain length.

The binary path already applies `Scan::Delta` and `Scan::OldOnly`. Restrict factorization to full-delta rounds:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 if runtime.factors.len() > 1
     && matches!(strategy, JoinStrategy::Planned)
+    && entry.delta == Delta::all(snapshot.rel.row_count())
 {
     return factors::evaluate(entry, snapshot, &mut governor);
 }
```

Add a regression test for a recursive rule with an independent ground positive atom over a long chain. Compare planned evaluation with `JoinStrategy::ForcedBinary` and assert that the planned path does not exceed the join-step limit.
</details>
